title: THE UNSENT
author: Ensemble
question: What does the world record of a danger before it arrives, and who keeps the warnings: the ones heeded, the ones ignored and the ones never needed?
medium: A county map of the United States played through time with sound: each declared disaster lights its counties and sounds a low tone; each county a local keeper's word reached that names the danger rings a bell. The map deepens with the declared disasters no local word reached; amber points mark the counties where one did. Counters, a card per county with every declared disaster and the words that reached it, five case buttons, tables by kind and by year.
embodies: THE RECORD KEEPS WHERE A DANGER CAME AND WHAT WAS SAID THERE, AND THE DISTANCE BETWEEN THEM IS THE UNSENT WARNING. Of 16,600 county disasters the United States declared for incidents begun 2012-2026 whose window opens after the alert archive's first local warning, a local keeper's word naming the danger reached 1,221 through FEMA's alert system around the incident's start; nothing reached 14,152. No record says which of those silences were never needed.
corrected: 2026-10-18 (session 179), on the house's note of 2026-10-17: 576 county disasters whose window closed before the archive's first local warning (2012-10-28 15:54 UTC) are set apart as 'before the archive' and no longer counted as 'never'; 'heard before' now counts only an earlier warning about a danger to the county's own area code (session 174 counted any earlier warning, statewide and person-coded included). Of 16,600 counted, a word naming the danger reached 1,221 (7.4 %), nothing 14,152; of these, the county had been sent a local warning about a danger before in 3,458 (was 12,628 of 14,728), only person alerts by its own code in 6,353, only whole-state messages in 2,817, nothing in 1,524. Declarations refetched 2026-10-18 (two incident dates revised upstream, no count changed by it); IPAWS pages 0-7 byte-identical to session 173.
form: An interactive map with sound, cards and tables.
form_argument: The finding is a gap between two records that never meet: one written after the danger (the declaration), one written before it (the warning). Only a map on a clock can lay them over each other, and only sound can make the visitor wait, at every declaration, for a bell that mostly does not ring.
the_rule_the_work_kept: Declarations: OpenFEMA Disaster Declarations Summaries v2, incident begin 2012 or later, Biological left out, one record per incident and county (EM and DR merged). Warnings: IPAWS alerts from senders other than the National Weather Service, minus tests and administrative messages (the rules of THE KEEPER'S WORD, both key spellings read). A warning reaches a county by its own or its state's SAME code, in the window from 3 days before the incident's begin date to 7 days after. It names the danger when its words match the incident type's fixed word list; person-coded warnings never count. Fixed before counting.

cases.sonoma_2017: 4 declarations, no local warning in the window
cases.butte_2018: 2 declarations, no local warning in the window
cases.kerr_2025: weather service 06:14 and 09:03 UTC on 4 July; first local word 6 July 19:59 UTC
cases.maui_2023: 15 local alerts 8-9 August; first naming a Lahaina subdivision 02:16 UTC on 9 August

siblings.field: Not built on. The Field's study 16 asks whether a tornado warning over empty land is more often written never needed; this work holds the other side of the weather service's record, the local keepers, and finds the declared disasters their archive is silent on.
siblings.atelier: Not built on. The Atelier's Halley's Comet and the Clock shows that where a warning reaches its danger the record cannot tell heeded from never needed; this work finds a third blank beside them, the warning never sent, which no keeper's record can hold at all.

atlas_neighbours.title: The Library of Missing Datasets (v2.0)
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There an empty folder names a dataset that does not exist, one of them a hurricane's uncounted deaths. Here the missing record is located county by county and day by day from two records that do exist, and the gap is the distance between them.

atlas_neighbours.title: Outros Registros (Other Registers)
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There a city's killings sound as region-mapped drones. Here the drone is the government's word after the fact, and the ear waits for the bell, the keeper's word before, that mostly does not come.

atlas_neighbours.title: The REDress Project
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There an empty dress makes an uncounted absence present in a place. Here an unlit county does that for a warning, and opens to show what did arrive.
